fillers.date_of_birth: the date of birth on file
fillers.name: Alex Martin

kind: in-scope: PII inside third-party document contexts
reconstruct: attack  = template with the target slot replaced by a cleared synthetic vector and every other slot by its filler; control_decoy = the SAME sentence with that vector replaced by a same-shape checksum-INVALID decoy; control_removed = the SAME sentence with that vector replaced by a neutral phrase. Attack and control differ by exactly the token.

sampling.protocol: rules may be written against dev; holdout is scored once, rules frozen
sampling.rule: every upstream template carrying a claimed or declared-out-of-scope placeholder is kept; split by TEMPLATE: first nibble of sha256(template), 0-7 -> dev, 8-f -> holdout
sampling.why: the template is what a rule meets, and one template materialises into as many cases as its category has vectors — so splitting the CASES would put the same template on both sides and a rule written on dev would score on holdout by identity, not by generalisation

source.what: PII detection evaluation and data-generation toolkit

strength: external contexts, author-cleared synthetic values — the DOCUMENTS are third-party, the VALUES are limes's own already-admitted vectors (ADR 0009 forbids any other kind). Strictly weaker than garak, where the attack itself is foreign. Labelled wherever published.
